notes:
CW-030 (Ravenwood Garden Company, Madison - a healthy garden centre selling plants, hard goods, install work and design) is the first N=4 run, and it splits the per-line COGS question cleanly down the middle.

The proposal half works, and it is the best single moment the campaign has produced. From one plain description the confidence gate named all four streams back, and at the COGS stage it opened with 'Your lines of business earn differently, so I am setting up direct costs separately for each' and then gave four distinct bands correctly ordered across the entire range - Design consult 6 percent on a 3-9 band, Install project 38 on 30-45, Plant sale 55 on 50-60, Hard goods sale 60 on 55-65 - plus the blend, the dollar total, and an explicit invitation to correct any one alone or collapse those that match.

Nothing below the proposal accepts a client value. The client corrected all four in one message, then one line alone mid-stage, then one line alone using the app's own line name and a bare percent. Six attempts, three phrasings, and cogs_percent_of_line_revenue read null on all four rows after every one. The cogs_shared collapse was acknowledged in precisely the right words - 'I will keep one shared direct-cost rate for Plant sale and Hard goods sale, with separate rates for Install project and Design consult' - and stored nothing. And the workbook carries a single flat 0.47 cost-of-goods row against total revenue rather than four rows summing to a total, which the grid confirms exactly.

The contrast within the same build is the useful part. sections.revenue has twelve driver rows - capacity, price and utilisation for each of the four lines, every value the client's own - and the mid-flow install capacity correction from 6 to 8 reached the workbook at 104.01 per quarter. Revenue is fully per-line at N=4. Cost is not per-line at all below the sentence that proposes it.

Everything else held. The goal anchor fired verbatim as a structured milestone. The owner was captured as one row with no phantom, cleaner than CW-029. A healthy business passed clean for the third run running, and section 6 came in 10/10 on a fourth consecutive build. Four candidate findings were dropped against the contract before filing - including the driver broadcast to not-yet-asked lines, which earlier runs would have filed as a bug and which the contract classes as an intermediate state.

recommendations.business: any business with more than one revenue line
recommendations.why: BLOCKER, and it is one cause with two faces. The per-line COGS proposal is excellent and the schema field exists - cogs_percent_of_line_revenue is present on every product row - but no client correction reaches it. Six attempts across three phrasings, including the app's own suggested form, all left it null, so an accepting client ships the app's blended guess: 0.47 here against the 0.406 the client's four figures actually imply, about 98,700 a year of cost they corrected away from. The second face is the workbook, which carries one flat cost-of-goods row against total revenue rather than four rows summing to a total. Revenue is fully per-line in the same build, so the shape to copy already exists one section over. Fix the write door and the model row together - separately they each leave the feature unusable.

recommendations.business: any multi-line business where two lines share economics
recommendations.why: MAJOR. The COGS proposal invites the collapse in as many words - 'if the costs really run about the same across lines, say so and I will treat them as one' - and the collapse is where client control over the distinct-COGS count lives. Asked for it, the first attempt was not understood and the second was acknowledged perfectly and stored nothing: no sharing flag anywhere in the operating model. Depends on A-110, since there is nowhere to write a shared rate until per-line rates exist. Worth noting the first refusal ASKED rather than guessing, which is the right failure.

MAJOR, and a clean instance of the rule the contract already states. One turn produced two receipts for values that were never stored: 'I will use a marketing budget of 0 a year (0 percent of revenue). Also recorded: cogs percent of revenue 0.' marketing_total_year1 read undefined rather than 0, and cogs_percent_of_revenue stayed 0.47, so nothing was corrupted - but a client reading that turn believes their marketing budget is now zero, and the zero was never theirs. Same family as the CW-028 receipts; worth checking whether they share a code path.

recommendations.business: any business that takes a price or rate lever and then builds
recommendations.why: PROBE STILL NEVER REACHED, four attempts running. Retention-applied has not been exercised end to end: CW-027 asked and did not apply the answer, and CW-028, CW-029 and CW-030 were never asked because each business passed without needing a lever. Three consecutive healthy shapes have now made it unreachable by accident. It needs a business priced below its market that clears its wall on a price lever and goes on to build - design the run around that single requirement.

CARRIED FORWARD, and now the cheapest thing on the board by a wide margin. Section 6's field check has passed 10/10 on four consecutive builds, so that limb needs no further evidence. The other two have still never been run: the byte-equal rerun on a coherent draft, and derived-field healing on an old or dormant draft. Four clean built drafts now exist to test against and no new intake is required for either.

recommendations.business: any business that cannot cover its costs at its stated price
recommendations.why: CARRIED FORWARD, untested for eight runs. Three healthy businesses have now passed cleanly and honestly, each time arguing its own pass figure down to a named ceiling, which is strong counter-evidence on the honesty half. The unexercised half is still an underpriced business that reaches a verdict without correcting itself first. Pairs naturally with A-106 - one well-designed underpriced run could settle both.

closed_this_cycle.reason: Superseded and answered. The design ruling CW-029 asked for has shipped: the app now proposes per-line COGS with distinct bands and invites both correction and collapse. What remains is that none of it can be written or modelled, which is A-110 and A-111 rather than an open design question.
Not reproduced. No state note contradicted a value it had just quoted in this run.
